meta.title: Be a good neighbour to animals
meta.description: This month’s kindness tip, ten street neighbours and how to be kind to them, what to do if you find a hurt animal, and a pledge card you make on your device.

hero.title: Be a good neighbour to the animals on your street
hero.lead: Dogs, cats, cows, crows and squirrels share our streets every day. Here is how to look, learn and help, without getting too close.
hero.photoCaption: A street dog in a warm vest on a winter morning.

month.title: Kindness for every month
month.lead: Each month brings its own heat, rain, festivals or babies. Here is the tip for now, and the whole year below.
month.allLead: Open any month to read its tips.

neighbours.title: Meet the neighbours
neighbours.lead: Ten animals you can see from a window, a balcony or the school bus. Read the fact, then flip the card to learn how to be a good neighbour.
neighbours.rule: The rule for every card: look and learn. Don’t touch, chase or feed by hand.
neighbours.flip: How to be a good neighbour
neighbours.flipLabel: How to be a good neighbour to the {name}

street.caption: Ten neighbours share this street. Tap or click a ring to meet one.

helps.title: Kind on the inside, helpful on the outside
helps.lead: Some kind ideas hurt animals by mistake. Swap them for these.

milk.try: a bowl of fresh water. Most grown-up cats can’t digest milk.

bread.try: a wide, shallow bowl of water. Change it every day.

sweets.try: putting food waste in a closed bin, never in plastic on the street.

chick.instead: picking up a baby bird on the ground
chick.try: leaving it be. Its parents are usually close by, watching.

holi.instead: Holi colours on a dog, even “safe” ones
holi.try: keeping colours for people. No colours on animals at all.

manja.try: plain cotton thread, and picking up loose string after.

hurt.eyebrow: If you find a hurt or scared animal
hurt.title: Stop, step back, tell a grown-up
hurt.lead: You don’t have to fix it yourself. The kindest thing a child can do is get the right grown-up.
hurt.grownUps: For grown-ups: what to do next
hurt.saveTitle: Save a number before you need it
hurt.saveBody: India has no single animal rescue helpline. Ask a vet, your municipality or a recognised animal welfare organisation for your nearest rescue’s number, save it in your phone, and check that it works.
hurt.save1962: Many states run 1962 for cattle and other livestock; hours vary by state. 112 is for people in danger, not for animals.
hurt.biteTitle: If an animal bites or scratches you
hurt.biteKid: Tell a grown-up right away. Wash it with soap and running water for 15 minutes. See a doctor the same day.

law.title: Caring is also a duty
law.kid: In India, hurting an animal on purpose is against the law. Anyone who looks after an animal must keep it well.
law.detail1: Section 3 of the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960 puts a duty of care on every person in charge of an animal. Section 11 lists acts of cruelty, such as beating, overloading and abandoning animals.
law.detail2: Article 51A(g) of the Constitution lists compassion for living creatures among every citizen’s fundamental duties. It is a value to practise, not a right a court enforces.
law.readAct: Read the Act on India Code

pledge.title: Make your kindness pledge card
pledge.lead: Pick a street neighbour and a promise. Your card is made right here on your device, ready to print or pin up.
pledge.name: Your first name or nickname

promises.water: keep a water bowl clean and change it every day
promises.distance: watch animals from far away and never chase them
promises.grownUp: tell a grown-up when I see a hurt animal
promises.thread: fly kites only with plain cotton thread
promises.bin: put food waste in a closed bin
promises.nests: leave nests, eggs and babies alone

pledge.privacy: Your card stays on this device. Nothing is sent to us or saved.
